newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on local dollar supply.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on local dollar supply.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed a quiet session on Monday slightly firmer across the board after dealers sold dollars to square positions, traders said.
"Dollars are still in supply in the market, which in today's case was due to locals squaring positions," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 0.5 centavos firmer, at 7.7980/7.8030 and 7.7940/7.8000 per dollar.
There were no same-day peso trades as the U.S. bond market was closed all day and foreign exchange trading closed early for Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

"The market was really dead. Greenspan speaks tomorrow, so let's see if that hits the long bond," another trader said, referring to U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to be given to the Senate Budget Committee on Tuesday.
